title: Mecka Raises $60 Million Series B Led By Sequoia Capital
key_facts: Mecka raised $60 million in Series B funding led by Sequoia Capital.
New investors include Nvidia, M12 (Microsoft's venture fund), Qualcomm Ventures and Samsung.
Mecka builds a data and deployment layer for robotics: its own multi-sensor capture hardware and global capture fleets that record human demonstrations such as gripping, folding and pouring.
It says robot development is limited more by lack of physical-world data than by hardware.
The company says it supplies data to several frontier robotics labs and says it passed $100 million in run-rate revenue in June 2026.
It expects about $300 million run-rate revenue by the end of 2026.
It is expanding into commercial robot deployment for enterprises without in-house robotics teams.
quote_evidence: Mecka raised $60 million in Series B funding led by Sequoia Capital to scale its robotics data infrastructure, expand its research efforts, and grow commercial robot deployments.
The company said it surpassed $100 million in run-rate revenue in June 2026, only a few months after beginning operations.
Mecka expects its run-rate revenue to reach approximately $300 million by the end of 2026.
why_it_matters_hint: Investors are paying to solve the shortage of real-world movement data for training robots.
notes: Reads like a company announcement; all revenue figures are the company's own. Not a machine doing something (funding story).
